title: The Coin Comes Home
overall_style: original intimate cinematic lullaby, restrained Thai atmosphere without quoting any existing song
tonal_center: D minor colors resolving gently toward F major
mix_notes: instrumental only, no vocals and no percussion; sparse enough to preserve coin, rain and paper foley; begin immediately but quietly; one coherent three-note motif; no trailer impacts; natural warm ending by 30 seconds

segments.music: three widely spaced felt-piano notes introduce a simple original lullaby-like motif; a nearly inaudible warm string harmonic arrives after the first breath
segments.sync: leave acoustic space around the coin contact at 4.10 seconds; let one high piano overtone answer it rather than striking on top of it

segments.emotion: solitary realization after learning the weight of earning
segments.music: move the same three-note motif into a lower felt-piano register with restrained suspended harmony; add only an airy wooden-flute breath texture, not a lead melody
segments.sync: darken gently with the rainy Bangkok cut at 7.0 seconds; keep the midrange open for rain and paper movements at 10.25, 12.15 and 13.35 seconds

segments.emotion: role reversal, gratitude and quiet resolve
segments.music: return the opening motif one octave higher; warm strings widen gradually beneath it and the harmony turns toward hope without becoming triumphant
segments.sync: recognize the visual rhyme at 16.0 seconds; reserve the strongest but still restrained harmonic bloom for the envelope touching the mother's palm at 20.25 seconds

segments.music: release into a soft F-major-colored piano voicing; the airy texture recedes and one final felt-piano note rings naturally over warm strings
segments.sync: open space as jasmine appears at 23.0 seconds and as the Thai sentence fades in at 25.15 seconds; resolve between 28.8 and 29.6 seconds with no abrupt cutoff
